text: Narrator moves are what you do in the story to portray the world, and you can play them at any time. General moves: split the characters up or put them together; change someone's attitude towards them; put something they care about at risk; present them with a difficult decision; offer an opportunity, with or without a cost; turn their move back on them; ask a question; ask "What do you do?". Narrator character moves: award or deduct House Points; give them extra work; make something off limits to them; cast a spell on them. Story moves: show signs of an ongoing or future threat; introduce a new character, place, or threat.

When a player gets a 6- on a roll, you may play a Serious Consequence, a special Narrator move that makes things worse for whoever failed. You need not play one, but you must make some kind of Narrator move. Options: give the character a Condition (Scared, Angry, Stressed, Jealous, Embarrassed, Injured, Hexed, or Unconscious) that fits what is happening; discipline them (deduct points, detention, revoked privileges, notify parents, suspension, expulsion); take something away from them; hurt someone they care about; force them into an impossible situation; change someone's attitude towards them, negatively; expose their secret; let their Rival win.

Teachers, staff, and House prefects award points for achievements and deduct them for rule-breaking. Typical amounts: 5 points for trivial things, such as a correct answer in class (+) or not paying attention (-); 10 points for minor things, such as clever answers on assignments (+) or arriving late to class (-); 20 points for notable things, such as disobeying a teacher (-) or being out of bounds after hours (-); 50 points for major things, such as saving another student's life (+) or putting another student in danger (-). The list is a guide; teachers may award or deduct for other reasons.

When a character wants to do something they normally could not, or wants to change a roll to a 10+, they may mark a point of Luck to do it. Every character starts with 3 points of Luck, and all marked Luck is regained when a school year is completed.
When a character fails a roll, they mark 1 point of Experience. At 4 Experience they may take an Advancement, and then clear their marked Experience.

Take an Advancement when a character has marked 4 Experience or completes a school year. Options: upgrade a trait by +1 (up to twice, and no trait may exceed +3); gain a second Favourite Subject (once); learn a new spell from their Year (as often as you like); acquire a magical object (as often as you like); or regain 1 marked point of Luck (as often as you like).

When someone is a character's Friend or Rival, that character may add +1 to a roll to help or hinder them. Friends and Rivals can be other players' characters or Narrator characters. A Friend or Rival is only added or removed at the end of a session. A character may have up to 2 Friends and 1 Rival at a time.

A character can leave the story when all eight Conditions are marked and they roll Exit the Story (2d6 plus their highest trait). On a 10+ they return with every Condition cleared. On a 7 to 9 they return with only Unconscious cleared. On a 6 or less they leave the story: they may be expelled, fall into a coma, have their memory wiped, be driven mad, be sent to Azkaban, be killed outright, or exit another way, as the story makes most sense. Then the player makes a new witch or wizard and the Narrator introduces them into the story.

Unforgivable Curses cannot be learned at the start of play, by taking an Advancement, by completing a school year, or from a class. When a character casts one, the Narrator may play a Serious Consequence that happens to them as a result.

A healing spell can clear the Injured, Hexed, or Unconscious Conditions if the spell's effect would heal the cause of the Condition. A defence spell can prevent someone from taking a Condition if the spell's effect would block the cause of the Condition. The Injured, Hexed, or Unconscious Conditions can always be cleared in the hospital wing.
When a character spends time with their pet, they may shift one marked Condition to another one.
A character's Patronus is chosen at creation, but they can only cast the Charm once they have learned it, usually in Year 5.
